docs.text: Users must authenticate before accessing protected features. The backend issues JWT access tokens after successful login. These tokens expire after a short time. Refresh tokens allow users to obtain new access tokens without logging in again. Tokens are sent in the Authorization header of API requests.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Role-based access control enforces permissions at the API level. Each endpoint checks the user's role before processing the request.

Role Access Level Farmer USSD menus only Extension Worker Mobile app features only Supervisor Dashboard features within their scope Administrator Full system access

docs.title: Password Security
docs.text: Passwords are hashed using a strong one-way hashing algorithm before storage. When a user logs in, the backend hashes the submitted password and compares it to the stored hash. Passwords are never stored in plain text. Users can change their passwords through the authenticated change-password endpoint.

docs.title: Session Management
docs.text: Sessions expire after a period of inactivity. Users must log in again when their session expires. The dashboard and mobile app handle session expiry by redirecting to the login screen or refreshing the token.

docs.title: Data Security
docs.text: Data security protects information stored in the database and configuration files.

docs.title: Encryption at Rest
docs.text: Sensitive data such as passwords, PINs, and tokens are encrypted before being stored in the PostgreSQL database. This ensures that even if the database is accessed without authorization, the sensitive values cannot be read.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: All API keys, database URLs, and secrets are stored in environment variables. These values are never written into the source code. The .env files containing these values are excluded from version control using .gitignore. In production, environment variables are managed through the Heroku dashboard.

docs.title: Database Security
docs.text: The PostgreSQL database is protected by credentials that are only known to the backend application. Direct database access is restricted. The database runs on a managed service that handles patching, backups, and network isolation.

docs.title: Backup and Recovery
docs.text: The database is backed up regularly. In the event of data loss or corruption, backups can be restored. The backup strategy ensures that critical agricultural data is not permanently lost.

docs.title: Webhook Security
docs.text: Webhooks are HTTP callbacks sent by external services to the backend. The platform receives webhooks from Africa's Talking for USSD sessions and SMS delivery status.

docs.title: Webhook Verification
docs.text: Webhook endpoints should verify that requests come from the expected sender. This can be done using signature verification or IP allowlisting where supported by the external service.

docs.title: HTTPS Webhooks
docs.text: Webhook URLs must use HTTPS. Africa's Talking requires publicly reachable HTTPS endpoints. For local development, a tunneling service such as ngrok can provide a temporary public URL.

docs.title: Input Sanitization
docs.text: Webhook endpoints validate and sanitize incoming data before processing. They check that required fields are present and that values are within expected ranges.

docs.title: Physical Security
docs.text: Physical security is handled by the hosting providers.

docs.title: Heroku Infrastructure
docs.text: The backend runs on Heroku, a managed platform. Heroku handles the physical security of the servers, network equipment, and data centers. This includes access controls, surveillance, and environmental protections.

docs.title: Device Security
docs.text: Extension Workers are responsible for the physical security of their smartphones. Lost or stolen devices should be reported so that accounts can be deactivated. The mobile app stores authentication tokens securely, but physical access to an unlocked device could allow unauthorized use.

docs.title: Incident Response
docs.text: An incident is any event that compromises the security or availability of the platform.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text: Incidents are detected through monitoring and logging. The backend logs errors and important events. Failed authentication attempts, unusual API activity, and external service failures are logged for investigation.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: When an incident is detected, the team investigates the cause and scope. Affected accounts may be suspended. Vulnerabilities are patched. If data is compromised, affected users are notified.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text: After an incident is contained, the team restores normal operations. This may involve rolling back to a previous stable release, restoring from backups, or reconfiguring security settings.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: All incidents are documented. The documentation includes what happened, how it was discovered, what actions were taken, and what measures were implemented to prevent recurrence.

docs.title: Risk Management
docs.text: Risk management is the ongoing process of identifying and reducing security risks.

docs.title: Dependency Management
docs.text: Third-party libraries and frameworks are kept up to date. Security patches are applied promptly. Outdated dependencies are reviewed regularly.

docs.title: Access Reviews
docs.text: User access is reviewed periodically. Accounts for users who no longer need access are deactivated. Role assignments are checked to ensure they match current responsibilities.

docs.title: Code Review
docs.text: All code changes are reviewed before merging. Reviewers check for security issues such as exposed secrets, missing input validation, and improper access control.

docs.title: Penetration Testing
docs.text: The platform may undergo penetration testing to identify vulnerabilities that automated tools cannot find. Findings are addressed before they can be exploited.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: Security is an ongoing priority for IvhuRedu. The platform implements multiple layers of protection including network encryption, input validation, role-based access control, password hashing, and secure configuration management. All team members share responsibility for maintaining security by following the code standards, protecting credentials, and reporting suspicious activity.
